commands.title: Time tree
commands.description: Date the ancestors and estimate the clock rate from sampling dates.

settings.label: Alignment
settings.help: Aligned FASTA input, plain or compressed (`gz`, `bz2`, `xz`, `zst`); compression is detected by extension.
settings.more: Each `--alignment` file is one partition, numbered by its position in the list (1, 2, ...). Use `-` to read uncompressed FASTA from standard input; `-` may appear at most once.

settings.label: Tree
settings.help: Tree in Newick format.

settings.label: Newick dialect
settings.help: Newick dialect of the tree inputs (the tree and the reference topology)
settings.more: A dialect is a tree structure and an annotation convention, written as <structure>,<annotations>. The structure is classic (plain labels and branch lengths), enewick (hybrid nodes such as x#H1) or rich (eNewick with support and probability fields). The annotations are plain (comments are text), beast ([&key=value]), nhx ([&&NHX:key=value]) or mrbayes ([&B name value]). For example, enewick,beast reads networks with BEAST annotations and classic,nhx reads NHX trees. TreeTime reads trees only, so a network input is an error.

settings.label: Allow missing sequences
settings.help: Treat tree tips that have no sequence in the alignment as fully ambiguous (missing data) instead of aborting.
settings.more: Without this flag the run aborts when more than one third of the tips lack a sequence, because the alignment may not belong to the tree. Useful for per-CDS translations, where some samples have no peptide for a given CDS.

settings.label: Metadata
settings.help: Metadata table (CSV or TSV) with one row per sample
settings.more: `--metadata-id-columns` names the column that links a row to a tree tip. The other columns hold the data of the sample, such as its sampling date or its traits.

settings.label: Metadata id columns
settings.help: Candidate column name(s) holding the taxon identifier that links metadata to tree tips
settings.more: The first listed column that is present in the header is used. Matching is case-insensitive.

settings.label: Metadata delimiters
settings.help: Candidate field delimiter(s) for the metadata table
settings.more: The delimiter actually present in the file is used. Defaults to comma, tab, and semicolon.

settings.label: Date column
settings.help: Label of the column to be used as sampling date (auto-detected when omitted)

settings.label: Date format
settings.help: Format used to parse string sampling dates (numeric, ISO, and uncertain dates parse regardless)

settings.label: Sequence length
settings.help: Length of the sequences, used to calculate the expected variation of the branch lengths
settings.more: Required without `--alignment`, and applies only then: with an alignment, the run takes the length from the alignment.

settings.label: Alphabet
settings.help: Sequence alphabet
settings.more: When omitted, the alphabet is auto-detected from sequence content and falls back to `nuc` when detection is ambiguous.

settings.label: Zero based
settings.help: Report sequence positions counted from 0 instead of 1.
settings.more: Applies to the mutations in the comments of Newick and Nexus trees and to the positions of the homoplasy report. Auspice JSON, augur node data, and UShER MAT outputs count from 1, as their formats require. An input table with positions, such as `--drms`, is always counted from 1.

settings.label: Clock rate
settings.help: If specified, the rate of the molecular clock won't be optimized.

settings.label: Clock rate std. dev.
settings.help: Standard deviation of the provided clock rate estimate
settings.more: Applies only with `--confidence`, whose date intervals include the clock rate uncertainty.

settings.label: Relaxed clock (slack, coupling)
settings.help: use an autocorrelated molecular clock. Strength of the gaussian priors on branch specific rate deviation and the coupling of parent and offspring rates can be specified e.g. as --relax 1.0 0.5. Values around 1.0 correspond to weak priors, larger values constrain rate deviations more strongly. Coupling 0 (--relax 1.0 0) corresponds to an un-correlated clock.

settings.label: Clock filter
settings.help: Ignore tips that do not follow a loose clock: the number of interquartile ranges from the root-to-tip regression beyond which a tip is an outlier.
settings.more: 0 switches the filter off.

settings.label: Allow negative rate
settings.help: Allow negative clock rates.
settings.more: By default, rates are forced to be positive. For trees with little temporal signal, removing this restriction gives essentially mid-point rooting.

settings.label: Branch length mode

options.help: `input` without an alignment or when the longest input branch is longer than 0.1 substitutions per site, `marginal` otherwise
Keep the branch lengths of the input tree
Estimate the branch lengths from the alignment by marginal ancestral reconstruction

settings.help: How the branch lengths of the time inference are obtained
settings.more: `auto` keeps the input branch lengths without an alignment, and also when the longest input branch is longer than 0.1 substitutions per site, because the re-estimated branch lengths are accurate only at short evolutionary distances; otherwise it re-estimates them as `marginal` does. When no input branch has a length, `auto` chooses `marginal`. The run logs the choice.

settings.label: Iterations
settings.help: Maximum number of iterations of the inference loop
settings.more: Polytomy resolution and coalescent models of the time inference need at least 2 iterations.

settings.label: No indels
settings.help: Disable indel (insertion and deletion) contributions to branch-length optimization and branch-length distributions.
settings.more: When set, branch-length optimization uses the substitution-only likelihood, and the branch distributions of the time inference exclude the Poisson indel term. This matches standard phylogenetic tools (RAxML, IQ-TREE, PhyML, BEAST) and TreeTime 0.x. By default, indels count.

settings.label: Confidence
settings.help: Estimate the 90% intervals of the node dates
settings.more: Runs a final marginal round of the time inference after the iterations and writes the 90% interval of every dated node. The intervals include the clock rate uncertainty when one is known: `--clock-std-dev` for a given rate, or the Gaussian estimate of an estimated rate. The rate uncertainty is added by inferring the dates again at the rate plus and minus one standard deviation and combining both parts in quadrature.

settings.label: Max grid points
settings.help: Largest number of points of one probability grid during time inference.
settings.more: A run stops with an error when a grid would need more points. The value bounds single grids, not the total memory of a run. When unset, the run takes the limit of the app or server that runs it, otherwise 1000000.

settings.label: Keep polytomies
settings.help: Keep the polytomies of the input tree
settings.more: Without this flag, each polytomy is resolved into binary mergers by the node dates. The resolution is stochastic: the run logs the seed it draws, and `--seed` reproduces the run.

settings.label: Coalescent prior
settings.help: Coalescent prior: a fixed time scale in substitutions per site (as in TreeTime 0.x and augur, for example 0.01) or as a time (10y, 26w, 90d); opt fits a constant time scale; skyline fits a piecewise-constant one
settings.more: A time is a positive number directly followed by the unit y (years), w (weeks) or d (days). A time scale in substitutions per site is converted to years with the clock rate of each iteration. Without this setting the node times have no coalescent prior.

settings.label: Skyline grid points
settings.help: Number of grid points in skyline coalescent model.
settings.more: Applies only to --coalescent skyline. Defines how many piecewise linear segments are used to model Tc(t) over time. Must be at least 2.

settings.label: Skyline stiffness
settings.help: Smoothing stiffness for the skyline coalescent.
settings.more: Penalizes log-fold-changes of the coalescent time scale Tc between adjacent skyline segments: with z = ln Tc, the objective adds `(stiffness/2) * Σ (ln(Tc_{i+1}/Tc_i))^2`. Because it acts on log Tc, the stiffness is dimensionless and scale-independent. Larger values enforce a smoother Tc(t). Applies only to --coalescent skyline.

settings.label: Coalescent confidence
settings.help: Confidence level for coalescent time scale (Tc) bands, in standard deviations.
settings.more: Applies only to the inferred coalescent priors (--coalescent opt and --coalescent skyline). The band spans `Tc * exp(±confidence * σ)`, where `σ` is the standard deviation of `ln Tc` from the coalescent likelihood curvature. A fixed time scale is not inferred and therefore has no band.

settings.label: Gen per year
settings.help: Generations per year for converting the coalescent time scale Tc into an effective population size.
settings.more: The coalescent output reports an effective population size `N_e = Tc * gen_per_year`. Tc is already in calendar years, so this factor rescales it into generation units, the standard axis of a skyline plot. Only affects the reported `N_e`; it does not enter the inference. Applies only with `--coalescent`.

settings.label: Reroot method
settings.help: Reroot the tree by temporal-signal optimization.
settings.more: Without a rooting setting the tree is rerooted by least-squares. Use --outgroup to root on named tips, or --keep-root to keep the input root.

settings.label: Outgroup
settings.help: Root the tree on the branch above the most recent common ancestor of the named tips
settings.more: With one tip, the root is placed on the branch leading to that tip.

settings.label: Keep root
settings.help: Keep the root of the input tree instead of rerooting it.

settings.label: Substitution model

options.help: Infer GTR parameters from data via Fitch parsimony substitution counts.

settings.help: Substitution model to use
settings.more: `infer` infers a model from the data of each partition; each `--alignment` file is one partition. Alternatively, name the model type. If the named model takes parameters, use `--model-params` to set them.

settings.label: Model params
settings.help: Parameters for the model selected by `--model`, given as space-separated `key=value` items
settings.more: The parameters apply to the model of every partition; each `--alignment` file is one partition. Keys: `mu` (the overall substitution rate, every named model), `kappa` (the transition to transversion ratio of `k80`, `hky85` and `t92`), `kappa1` and `kappa2` (the rate ratios of `tn93`), `pi` (the equilibrium frequencies of `f81`, `hky85` and `tn93`: comma-separated numbers, one frequency per state of the alphabet in its order, for example A, C, G and T for nucleotides, normalized to sum 1; also `pis`, `Pi`, `Pis`) and `pi_GC` (the GC content of `t92`, between 0 and 1). A key left out keeps its default. Example: `--model hky85 --model-params kappa=0.2 pis=0.25,0.25,0.25,0.25`.

settings.label: Partition rates

options.help: Estimate one relative rate per partition, normalized to a site-weighted mean of 1.
Fix the relative rate of every partition at 1.

settings.help: Relative substitution rates of the partitions
settings.more:
Each `--alignment` file is one partition. With two or more partitions, all partitions share the branch lengths, and each partition has one relative rate that scales them for the sites of that partition. `estimate` fits the rate of each partition with the rest of its substitution model fixed (a partition with `--model infer` starts from its fitted rate), then divides all rates by their mean weighted by the number of sites of each partition, so that this mean is 1. The branch lengths are then expected substitutions per site, averaged over all sites of all partitions. `equal` fixes the rate of every partition at 1.

The setting applies only with two or more partitions.

settings.label: Representation

options.help: Let TreeTime choose the representation; it chooses sparse
Probabilities of every state at every alignment position
Only the variable positions

settings.help: Representation of the sequences on the tree
settings.more: The dense representation stores the probabilities of every state at every alignment position of each node; the sparse representation stores only the variable positions. Dense is more accurate when branches are long and many sites change, but uses more memory.

settings.label: Gap fill
settings.help: How to handle gap characters in input sequences
settings.more: 'only-terminal': replace leading and trailing gap characters with the ambiguous character (default, matches v0). 'all': replace all gap characters with the ambiguous character. 'none': leave all gap characters unchanged.

settings.label: Include leaves
settings.help: Emit reconstructed leaf (tip) sequences in addition to internal nodes.

settings.label: Reconstruct tip states
settings.help: Same as `--include-leaves --impute-missing-data`: emit tip sequences with ambiguous and unknown states resolved to the most likely inferred state.

settings.label: Report ambiguous
settings.help: Include branch mutations from or to the fully ambiguous state (`N` for nucleotides, `X` for amino acids).
settings.more: By default these mutations are omitted from the branch mutations of the Newick and Nexus annotations, the Auspice JSON, and the `muts` and `aa_muts` lists of augur node data. Other ambiguity codes, such as `K` or `R`, are always reported. The flag does not affect the MAT outputs, which store `N` as missing data and never contain these mutations.

settings.label: Impute missing data
settings.help: Resolve ambiguous and unknown tip states (`N` and IUPAC codes such as `R`) to the most likely inferred state.
settings.more: Gaps are left as deletions, because they are inferred structure, not missing data. Changes that involve ambiguous characters on terminal branches then disappear from the branch mutations. Only defined for marginal reconstruction; a no-op with a warning under `--method-anc=parsimony`.

settings.label: Divergence units
settings.help: Units of the divergence values in the augur node data and Auspice outputs.
settings.more: `mutations-per-site` (default): branch divergence as substitutions per site. `mutations`: count of reconstructed substitutions per branch that change the state: gaps, `N`, and ambiguity codes compatible with the parent state do not count. `mutations` requires reconstructed sequences, so it does not work with input branch lengths (`--branch-length-mode=input`).

settings.label: Output node data
settings.help: Path to output augur-compatible node data JSON.
settings.more:
Contains per-node dates, branch lengths, clock model parameters, confidence intervals, and divergence metrics. The output is compatible with augur export v2 --node-data for Nextstrain pipeline integration.

Takes precedence over paths configured with `--output-all` and `--output-selection`.

settings.label: Output model
settings.help: Path to output the fitted substitution models as JSON.
settings.more: Takes precedence over paths configured with `--output-all` and `--output-selection`.

settings.label: Output sequences
settings.help: Path to output the nucleotide sequences of the nodes as FASTA.
settings.more:
Holds the reconstructed sequences of the internal nodes, and of the tips with `--include-leaves` or `--reconstruct-tip-states`; `--impute-missing-data` resolves ambiguous tip states. Takes precedence over paths configured with `--output-all` and `--output-selection`.

With several `--alignment` files, one file is written per alignment, and the file name must contain `{alignment}`, which is replaced by the number of the alignment (1, 2, ...).

settings.label: Output clock model
settings.help: Path to output clock model JSON.
settings.more: Takes precedence over paths configured with `--output-all` and `--output-selection`.

settings.label: Output root-to-tip
settings.help: Path to output the root-to-tip regression table.
settings.more: One row per sample: the date the regression used, the root-to-tip distance it regressed on, the date the clock model predicts from that distance, and whether the clock filter excluded the sample. Takes precedence over paths configured with `--output-all` and `--output-selection`.

settings.label: Output confidence TSV
settings.help: Path to output date-confidence-interval TSV.
settings.more: Takes precedence over paths configured with `--output-all` and `--output-selection`.

settings.label: Output tracelog
settings.help: Path to output the convergence values of every iteration as a table.
settings.more: Takes precedence over paths configured with `--output-all` and `--output-selection`.

settings.label: Output coalescent
settings.help: Path to output the coalescent time scale as a table (one row per skyline segment).
settings.more: Written when a coalescent prior is set with `--coalescent`. A fixed time scale writes one band-less segment over the tree span. Takes precedence over paths configured with `--output-all` and `--output-selection`.

settings.label: Output coalescent JSON
settings.help: Path to output the coalescent time scale as a rich JSON document (inputs + segments).
settings.more: Written when a coalescent model is set. Takes precedence over paths configured with `--output-all` and `--output-selection`.

settings.label: Output all
settings.help: Write all default output files into this directory.
settings.more:
Produces the default set of tree and non-tree outputs for the command, using `<dir>/<command>.<ext>` paths. Combine with `--output-selection` to restrict which outputs are written.

Per-file flags (`--output-tree-nwk`, `--output-node-data`, etc.) override or supplement the files produced by `--output-all`.

An output that the run has no data for is skipped without a message, for example the substitution model of a run that fits none. A per-file flag for such an output fails.

Table outputs choose the delimiter by the extension of their path: `.tsv` writes tabs and `.csv` commas, also before a compression suffix (`dates.tsv.gz`); `-` writes tabs to standard output. Default names use `.tsv`.

With several `--alignment` files, the outputs that carry sequence positions are written once per file: reconstructed sequences, the augur node data of `ancestral`, Auspice, UShER MAT, Nexus, and Newick with `--newick-annotations` other than `plain`. Files are numbered 1, 2, ... in the order of the `--alignment` list. Their default names carry the number after the command name (`<dir>/<command>.1.<ext>`), and the file name of a per-file flag for such an output must contain `{alignment}`, which is replaced by the number. Other tree outputs with `{alignment}` in their file name are also written once per file.

An output path that ends in `.gz`, `.bz2`, `.xz`, or `.zst` writes a compressed file. The compression level is 2, unless the environment variable `GZ_COMPRESSION`, `BZ2_COMPRESSION`, `XZ_COMPRESSION`, or `ZST_COMPRESSION` sets another level. `.gz`, `.xz`, and `.zst` compress with all `--jobs` threads. `.bz2` compresses with one thread and is much slower to write and to read than the other formats.

settings.label: Newick annotations
settings.help: Node comments of the Newick outputs: `plain`, `beast`, or `nhx`.
settings.more: `plain` writes no comments. `beast` writes a comment such as `[&mutations="A45G,G136T",date=2016.45]` after each node, and `nhx` writes the same values as `[&&NHX:key=value]`. The comments hold the mutations on the branch above the node, its date, and its inferred trait value, as far as the command infers them. Nexus outputs always carry `beast` comments, which FigTree reads.

settings.label: Output tree Newick
settings.help: Path to output Newick tree file.
settings.more:
Takes precedence over paths configured with `--output-all` and `--output-selection`. `--newick-annotations` sets the node comments.

With several `--alignment` files and `--newick-annotations` other than `plain`, one file is written per alignment, and the file name must contain `{alignment}`, which is replaced by the number of the alignment (1, 2, ...).

Compression: path ending in `.gz`, `.bz2`, `.xz`, `.zst` writes compressed output. Use `-` to write uncompressed to stdout.

Parent directories are created if missing.

settings.label: Output tree nexus
settings.help: Path to output Nexus tree file.
settings.more:
Takes precedence over paths configured with `--output-all` and `--output-selection`. The nodes carry BEAST comments (`[&mutations="A45G,G136T",date=2016.45]`).

With several `--alignment` files, one file is written per alignment, and the file name must contain `{alignment}`, which is replaced by the number of the alignment (1, 2, ...).

Compression: path ending in `.gz`, `.bz2`, `.xz`, `.zst` writes compressed output. Use `-` to write uncompressed to stdout.

Parent directories are created if missing.

settings.label: Output tree auspice
settings.help: Path to output Auspice v2 JSON tree file.
settings.more:
Takes precedence over paths configured with `--output-all` and `--output-selection`.

With several `--alignment` files, one file is written per alignment, and the file name must contain `{alignment}`, which is replaced by the number of the alignment (1, 2, ...).

Compression: path ending in `.gz`, `.bz2`, `.xz`, `.zst` writes compressed output. Use `-` to write uncompressed to stdout.

Parent directories are created if missing.

settings.label: Output tree MAT protobuf
settings.help: Path to output UShER MAT protobuf tree file.
settings.more:
Takes precedence over paths configured with `--output-all` and `--output-selection`.

With several `--alignment` files, one file is written per alignment, and the file name must contain `{alignment}`, which is replaced by the number of the alignment (1, 2, ...).

Compression: path ending in `.gz`, `.bz2`, `.xz`, `.zst` writes compressed output. Use `-` to write uncompressed to stdout.

Parent directories are created if missing.

settings.label: Output tree MAT JSON
settings.help: Path to output UShER MAT JSON tree file.
settings.more:
Takes precedence over paths configured with `--output-all` and `--output-selection`.

With several `--alignment` files, one file is written per alignment, and the file name must contain `{alignment}`, which is replaced by the number of the alignment (1, 2, ...).

Compression: path ending in `.gz`, `.bz2`, `.xz`, `.zst` writes compressed output. Use `-` to write uncompressed to stdout.

Parent directories are created if missing.

settings.label: Output tree graph JSON
settings.help: Path to output internal graph JSON tree file.
settings.more:
Takes precedence over paths configured with `--output-all` and `--output-selection`.

Compression: path ending in `.gz`, `.bz2`, `.xz`, `.zst` writes compressed output. Use `-` to write uncompressed to stdout.

Parent directories are created if missing.

settings.label: Output tree DOT
settings.help: Path to output Graphviz DOT tree file.
settings.more:
Takes precedence over paths configured with `--output-all` and `--output-selection`.

Compression: path ending in `.gz`, `.bz2`, `.xz`, `.zst` writes compressed output. Use `-` to write uncompressed to stdout.

Parent directories are created if missing.

settings.label: Output files
settings.help: List of outputs to produce with `--output-all`.
settings.more:
Restricts which outputs `--output-all` writes. Special value `all` expands to every output available for this command. Requires `--output-all`. Per-file flags are always honored regardless of this selection.

A selected output that the run has no data for is skipped without a message, for example the substitution model of a run that fits none. A per-file flag for such an output fails. An output that the settings rule out fails in both forms, for example the sequences of `timetree --branch-length-mode input`.

settings.label: Ambiguity threshold
settings.help: Report every state whose posterior probability is at most this far below the probability of the most likely state.
settings.more:
The value is a difference of probabilities from 0 to 1. With 0, the report names only the states that tie with the most likely state. RAxML-NG uses 0.5 divided by the number of states, for example 0.125 for nucleotides. The report is off when the value is not set.

The reconstructed FASTA writes a position with more than one reported state as the IUPAC code of these states, or `N` for all four nucleotides. Internal nodes have a report at every position, leaves only at the positions that `--impute-missing-data` imputes.

settings.label: Ambiguity outputs

options.help: Reconstructed nucleotide FASTA

settings.help: List of the outputs that carry the ambiguity report.
settings.more: Without this list, every output of the run that can carry the report carries it. Requires `--ambiguity-threshold`.

settings.label: Topology order
settings.help: Canonical topology ordering preset.

settings.label: Topology order tree
settings.help: Tree whose leaf order sets the target order
settings.more: Used by `--topology-order target-order` and `target-order-reverse`. Without this flag and `--topology-order-list`, the leaf order of the input tree is the target order.

settings.label: Topology order list
settings.help: File with leaf names in the target order, one name per line
settings.more: Used by `--topology-order target-order` and `target-order-reverse`. Without this flag and `--topology-order-tree`, the leaf order of the input tree is the target order.

settings.label: Topology order aggregate
settings.help: Aggregate used to map a subtree to a target-order position.

settings.label: Seed
settings.help: Random seed
settings.more: Without a seed, a run with a random step draws one and logs it, so the run can be reproduced.

options.help: Infer GTR parameters from data via Fitch parsimony substitution counts.

settings.help: Substitution model to use
settings.more: `infer` infers a model from the data of each partition; each `--alignment` file is one partition. Alternatively, name the model type. If the named model takes parameters, use `--model-params` to set them.

settings.label: Model params
settings.help: Parameters for the model selected by `--model`, given as space-separated `key=value` items
settings.more: The parameters apply to the model of every partition; each `--alignment` file is one partition. settings.label: Partition rates

options.help: Estimate one relative rate per partition, normalized to a site-weighted mean of 1.
Fix the relative rate of every partition at 1.

settings.help: Relative substitution rates of the partitions
settings.more:
Each `--alignment` file is one partition. With two or more partitions, all partitions share the branch lengths, and each partition has one relative rate that scales them for the sites of that partition. `estimate` fits the rate of each partition with the rest of its substitution model fixed (a partition with `--model infer` starts from its fitted rate), then divides all rates by their mean weighted by the number of sites of each partition, so that this mean is 1. The branch lengths are then expected substitutions per site, averaged over all sites of all partitions. `equal` fixes the rate of every partition at 1.

The setting applies only with two or more partitions.

Probabilities of every state at every alignment position
Only the variable positions

settings.help: Representation of the sequences on the tree
settings.more: The dense representation stores the probabilities of every state at every alignment position of each node; the sparse representation stores only the variable positions. Dense is more accurate when branches are long and many sites change, but uses more memory.

settings.label: Divergence units
settings.help: Units of the divergence values in the augur node data and Auspice outputs.
settings.more: `mutations-per-site` (default): branch divergence as substitutions per site. `mutations`: count of reconstructed substitutions per branch that change the state: gaps, `N`, and ambiguity codes compatible with the parent state do not count. `mutations` requires reconstructed sequences, so it does not work with input branch lengths (`--branch-length-mode=input`).

settings.label: Output node data
settings.help: Path to output augur-compatible node data JSON.
settings.more:
Contains per-node optimized branch lengths (divergence, substitutions per site) and the input alignment and tree paths. The output is compatible with augur export v2 --node-data.

Takes precedence over paths configured with `--output-all` and `--output-selection`.

settings.label: Output model
settings.help: Path to output the fitted substitution models as JSON.
settings.more: Takes precedence over paths configured with `--output-all` and `--output-selection`.

settings.label: Output files
settings.help: List of outputs to produce with `--output-all`.
settings.more:
Restricts which outputs `--output-all` writes. Special value `all` expands to every output available for this command. Requires `--output-all`. Per-file flags are always honored regardless of this selection.

A selected output that the run has no data for is skipped without a message, for example the substitution model of a run that fits none. A per-file flag for such an output fails. An output that the settings rule out fails in both forms, for example the sequences of `timetree --branch-length-mode input`.

settings.label: No indels
settings.help: Disable indel (insertion and deletion) contributions to branch-length optimization and branch-length distributions.
settings.more: When set, branch-length optimization uses the substitution-only likelihood, and the branch distributions of the time inference exclude the Poisson indel term. This matches standard phylogenetic tools (RAxML, IQ-TREE, PhyML, BEAST) and TreeTime 0.x. By default, indels count.

settings.label: Iterations
settings.help: Maximum number of iterations of the inference loop
settings.more: Polytomy resolution and coalescent models of the time inference need at least 2 iterations.

settings.label: Tolerance
settings.help: Likelihood convergence threshold. The loop stops when successive likelihoods differ by less than this value, or when a 2-cycle with amplitude below this value is detected.

settings.label: Damping
settings.help: Damping factor $d$ for outer-loop updates: $b=b_{new}(1-d)+b_{old}d$, where $d=max(damping^{i+1},0.01)$. Higher values reduce oscillation; zero disables damping. Must be in $[0,1)$.

settings.label: Initial branch lengths

options.help: Estimate only edges with missing or invalid branch lengths, preserve valid input values. No-op when all edges have finite branch lengths.
Estimate all edges, overwriting input branch lengths.
Use input branch lengths as-is. Fails if any edge has a missing or invalid branch length.

settings.help: Initial branch length estimate before the per-edge optimization.
settings.more: - auto: estimate only edges with missing or invalid branch lengths, preserve valid input values (default) - always: estimate all edges, overwriting input branch lengths - never: use input branch lengths as-is; fails if any are missing

settings.label: Optimizer

options.help: Brent's method in $\sqrt{t}$ space.
Newton-Raphson in $\sqrt{t}$ space.

settings.help: Per-edge optimizer. Both methods optimize in $\sqrt{t}$ space. Values are `brent` (default) and `newton`.

settings.label: No collapse zero branches
settings.help: Disable collapsing of internal branches whose optimized length is zero.
settings.more: By default the optimize loop contracts internal edges the per-edge optimizer drove to exactly zero that carry no substitutions or indels, turning the resulting binary nodes into polytomies. When set, such edges are kept in the output tree with length zero.

settings.label: No merge shared mutations
settings.help: Disable merging of polytomy siblings that share substitutions.
settings.more: By default, sibling branches in a polytomy that carry identical substitutions are grouped under a new internal node. The step and the flag apply only to the sparse representation.

settings.label: No hoist reversions
settings.help: Disable the reversion hoist in polytomies.
settings.more: By default, when a child branch carries the exact reversion of a substitution on the node's parent branch, a new node is inserted that groups the node with that child, removing one mutation per reverted position. When set, those reversions are left in place. The step and the flag apply only to the sparse representation.

settings.label: Topology order
settings.help: Canonical topology ordering preset.

settings.label: Topology order tree
settings.help: Tree whose leaf order sets the target order
settings.more: Used by `--topology-order target-order` and `target-order-reverse`. Without this flag and `--topology-order-list`, the leaf order of the input tree is the target order.

settings.label: Topology order list
settings.help: File with leaf names in the target order, one name per line
settings.more: Used by `--topology-order target-order` and `target-order-reverse`. Without this flag and `--topology-order-tree`, the leaf order of the input tree is the target order.

settings.label: Topology order aggregate
settings.help: Aggregate used to map a subtree to a target-order position.

settings.label: Reroot method
settings.help: Reroot the tree by minimizing root-to-tip divergence variance.
settings.more: By default, optimize keeps the input root. Pass --reroot=min-dev to enable divergence-based rerooting. Date-dependent methods (least-squares, oldest) are available in the timetree and clock commands.

settings.label: Outgroup
settings.help: Root the tree on the branch above the most recent common ancestor of the named tips
settings.more: With one tip, the root is placed on the branch leading to that tip.

settings.label: Keep root
settings.help: Keep the root of the input tree instead of rerooting it.

settings.label: Alignment
settings.help: Aligned FASTA input, plain or compressed (`gz`, `bz2`, `xz`, `zst`); compression is detected by extension.
settings.more: Each `--alignment` file is one partition, numbered by its position in the list (1, 2, ...). Use `-` to read uncompressed FASTA from standard input; `-` may appear at most once.

settings.label: Tree
settings.help: Tree in Newick format.

settings.label: Newick dialect
settings.help: Newick dialect of the tree inputs (the tree and the reference topology)
settings.more: A dialect is a tree structure and an annotation convention, written as <structure>,<annotations>. The structure is classic (plain labels and branch lengths), enewick (hybrid nodes such as x#H1) or rich (eNewick with support and probability fields). The annotations are plain (comments are text), beast ([&key=value]), nhx ([&&NHX:key=value]) or mrbayes ([&B name value]). For example, enewick,beast reads networks with BEAST annotations and classic,nhx reads NHX trees. TreeTime reads trees only, so a network input is an error.

settings.label: Allow missing sequences
settings.help: Treat tree tips that have no sequence in the alignment as fully ambiguous (missing data) instead of aborting.
settings.more: Without this flag the run aborts when more than one third of the tips lack a sequence, because the alignment may not belong to the tree. Useful for per-CDS translations, where some samples have no peptide for a given CDS.

settings.label: Alphabet
settings.help: Sequence alphabet
settings.more: When omitted, the alphabet is auto-detected from sequence content and falls back to `nuc` when detection is ambiguous.

settings.label: Zero based
settings.help: Report sequence positions counted from 0 instead of 1.
settings.more: Applies to the mutations in the comments of Newick and Nexus trees and to the positions of the homoplasy report. Auspice JSON, augur node data, and UShER MAT outputs count from 1, as their formats require. An input table with positions, such as `--drms`, is always counted from 1.

settings.label: Output all
settings.help: Write all default output files into this directory.
settings.more:
Produces the default set of tree and non-tree outputs for the command, using `<dir>/<command>.<ext>` paths. Combine with `--output-selection` to restrict which outputs are written.

Per-file flags (`--output-tree-nwk`, `--output-node-data`, etc.) override or supplement the files produced by `--output-all`.

An output that the run has no data for is skipped without a message, for example the substitution model of a run that fits none. A per-file flag for such an output fails.

Table outputs choose the delimiter by the extension of their path: `.tsv` writes tabs and `.csv` commas, also before a compression suffix (`dates.tsv.gz`); `-` writes tabs to standard output. Default names use `.tsv`.

With several `--alignment` files, the outputs that carry sequence positions are written once per file: reconstructed sequences, the augur node data of `ancestral`, Auspice, UShER MAT, Nexus, and Newick with `--newick-annotations` other than `plain`. Files are numbered 1, 2, ... in the order of the `--alignment` list. Their default names carry the number after the command name (`<dir>/<command>.1.<ext>`), and the file name of a per-file flag for such an output must contain `{alignment}`, which is replaced by the number. Other tree outputs with `{alignment}` in their file name are also written once per file.

An output path that ends in `.gz`, `.bz2`, `.xz`, or `.zst` writes a compressed file. The compression level is 2, unless the environment variable `GZ_COMPRESSION`, `BZ2_COMPRESSION`, `XZ_COMPRESSION`, or `ZST_COMPRESSION` sets another level. `.gz`, `.xz`, and `.zst` compress with all `--jobs` threads. `.bz2` compresses with one thread and is much slower to write and to read than the other formats.

settings.label: Newick annotations
settings.help: Node comments of the Newick outputs: `plain`, `beast`, or `nhx`.
settings.more: `plain` writes no comments. `beast` writes a comment such as `[&mutations="A45G,G136T",date=2016.45]` after each node, and `nhx` writes the same values as `[&&NHX:key=value]`. The comments hold the mutations on the branch above the node, its date, and its inferred trait value, as far as the command infers them. Nexus outputs always carry `beast` comments, which FigTree reads.

settings.label: Merge shared mutations
settings.help: Merge branches in polytomies that share identical mutations
settings.more:
When sibling branches in a polytomy (node with >2 children) carry identical substitutions, they are grouped under a new internal node. The shared mutations move to the new branch (parent to new node), and only unique mutations remain on children's edges. Reduces tree builder artifacts from arbitrary binary resolution of polytomies.

Requires --alignment
